learn.title: Stop time and look around
learn.body: A debugger runs your program under your control. You can pause it on any line, step one line at a time, and look at variables without editing the code. The usual ones are gdb on Linux and lldb on macOS.

learn.title: Build with -g
learn.body: The `-g` flag adds line information so the debugger can show your source. Then start the program under the debugger.
learn.code:
cc -g -std=c11 prog.c -o prog
lldb ./prog
# or: gdb ./prog

learn.title: Breakpoints
learn.body: A breakpoint is a place where the program pauses. `break main` (gdb) or `b main` (lldb) pauses at the start of `main`. `run` starts the program and it stops at the first breakpoint.

learn.title: Moving and looking
learn.body: `next` runs one line and skips over calls. `step` goes into a call. `print total` shows a variable. `continue` runs on. `quit` leaves. Short forms: `n`, `s`, `p`, `c`, `q`.
learn.code:
break main
run
next
print total
continue
quit

learn.title: A debugging session
steps: Build with `-g` and start the debugger
Press `next` and `print total` after each line
The first wrong value shows where the bug is

learn.body: If the program crashes, type `bt` to see the chain of calls that led there.

questions.prompt: Which flag lets the debugger show your source lines?
questions.explanation: `-g` adds debug information to the program.

choices: Pauses the program at that place
questions.explanation: You then inspect and step from there.

questions.prompt: Which command shows the value of a variable `total`? Type the long form with the variable.
questions.explanation: `print total` (short: `p total`) shows its current value.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `next` and `step`?
choices: `step` goes into a function call, `next` skips over it
questions.explanation: Use `step` when you want to look inside the function.

questions.prompt: Typing \_\_ makes the program run until the next breakpoint.
Match each command to what it does.
pairs: Pause at the start of main
questions.explanation: These four commands cover most sessions.

questions.prompt: Put a debugging session in order.
questions.explanation: You need the symbols first, then a stop point, then a run to reach it.
